item.title: PHP Methods to Set Custom HTTP Response Status Codes
item.description:
“PHP Methods to Set Custom HTTP Response Status Codes”

When developing web applications with PHP, accurately reporting the result of a request via the HTTP status code is crucial for client consumption and debugging. How does one reliably transmit a specific status code, such as a 404 Not Found or a custom code like 521 Web server is down, across different PHP environments (like standard mod_php, CGI, or FPM)? Several methods exist, each with its own compatibility constraints and environmental considerations.

item.title: Essential HTTP Header Flushing: When and Why to Use exit() After PHP header()
item.description:
“Essential HTTP Header Flushing: When and Why to Use exit() After PHP header()”

When employing PHP’s header() function to initiate an HTTP redirect, a critical question arises: Must the script execution be halted immediately afterward using exit() or die()? The consensus across various scenarios points toward this being highly advisable, though technically not always strictly mandated by the HTTP specification alone.

Is exit() Necessary After header("Location: ...")?

The simple answer is that while sending the header itself doesn’t automatically terminate the script, allowing execution to continue post-redirect is generally poor practice and can lead to unexpected behavior or security exposure.

item.title: Fixing X-Frame-Options: Why Iframes Get Blocked and Server-Side Solutions
item.description:
“Fixing X-Frame-Options: Why Iframes Get Blocked and Server-Side Solutions”

Why Can’t I Load Content in an Iframe? The Role of X-Frame-Options

The core issue stems from the HTTP response header X-Frame-Options, which is set by the server hosting the resource you are trying to load (e.g., google.com.ua in many examples). This header signals to the browser whether it is permissible to display the page within a frame on another site.
